item.title: China sends key signals to steady capital market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- A State Council executive meeting on Friday sent key signals from Chinese policymakers on steadying the capital market, with major stock indices surging after the meeting. The meeting, which studied work on further deepening comprehensive investment and financing reforms in the capital market, stressed that the capital market is vital to overall economic development. It called for fully leveraging the existing policies and underscored the need to mull and roll out new measures to promote the steady and sound development of the capital market. More than 5,000 stocks on China's A-share market traded higher on Friday, with a marked increase in the trading volume. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index closed 3.73 percent higher and the Shenzhen Component Index jumped 7.24 percent. Analysts took note of the meeting's clear positioning of the capital market within the overall framework of economic development, pointing out that the market concerns corporate financing and industrial upgrading as well as household assets and property income. "Stabilizing the stock market means stabilizing expectations, which is of great significance for consolidating the momentum of economic recovery and improvement," said Xie Yaxuan, head of the research and development center at China Merchants Securities. Official data showed that since early October, the amount of share repurchases and shareholding increases implemented by listed companies has reached nearly 60 billion yuan (about 8.9 billion U.S. dollars), far exceeding previous levels. Looking forward, there are greater market expectations for policies to support the capital market and the macroeconomy, analysts said. Friday's meeting emphasized that it is necessary to enhance the role of state-backed funds in stabilizing the market, and optimize the quasi-"stabilization fund" function of the state-owned Central Huijin Investment Ltd. to provide sufficient liquidity. Since early October, net subscriptions of equity exchange-traded funds have reached nearly 800 billion yuan, helping support major stock indices amid market fluctuations. Market observers predicted that the "national team" of state-backed funds will play a more prominent role in the market-stabilization mechanism in the future. The meeting also called for improving policies to support and guide medium- and long-term funds, including insurance funds, enterprise annuity funds and social security funds, to invest in the capital market. Institutional investors have been stepping up countercyclical investment. Publicly offered funds, securities firms' proprietary trading desks, private securities investment funds, social security funds and insurance institutions have all made net purchases of A-shares since early October. The meeting demanded strengthening the capacity to guard against and respond to external risks. This requires taking a coordinated approach to addressing domestic and external risks, said Liu Yu, chief economist at Industrial Securities. Since early October, global technology stocks have experienced sharp fluctuations at elevated levels, with volatility in overseas tech stocks causing a sustained impact on Chinese stocks. China's ChiNext Index, tracking the country's Nasdaq-style board of growth enterprises, has seen its trailing price-to-earnings ratio fall to a historic low. On Friday, the ChiNext Index surged 11.61 percent, while the STAR Composite Index, which reflects the performance of stocks on China's sci-tech innovation board, jumped 14.21 percent. Efforts are expected to strengthen cross-border risk monitoring and early-warning mechanisms as well as policy responses, while drawing on market-stabilization funds and medium- and long-term capital to bolster market resilience and prevent short-term external shocks from triggering sharp market swings, Liu said. ■

item.title: China launches new remote sensing satellite
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
A modified Long March-6 carrier rocket carrying the Yaogan-50 04 satellite blasts off from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province, Nov. 27, 2026. China launched a remote sensing satellite from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province on Friday. The Yaogan-50 04 satellite was launched at 9:05 p.m. (Beijing Time) aboard a modified Long March-6 carrier rocket and entered its planned orbit. The launch mission was a complete success. (Photo by Wang Yapeng/Xinhua) TAIYUAN, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- China launched a remote sensing satellite from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province on Friday. The Yaogan-50 04 satellite was launched at 9:05 p.m. (Beijing Time) aboard a modified Long March-6 carrier rocket and entered its planned orbit. The launch mission was a complete success. The satellite will primarily be used for land survey, crop yield estimation, and disaster prevention and relief. The launch marked the 682nd flight mission of the Long March carrier rocket series. ■ A modified Long March-6 carrier rocket carrying the Yaogan-50 04 satellite blasts off from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in north China's Shanxi Province, Nov. 27, 2026. item.title: China, ASEAN join forces to build stronger community with shared future
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
* Today, China and ASEAN have established 66 cooperation mechanisms across various fields and at all levels -- the highest number among all of ASEAN's dialogue partners, according to the Chinese Mission to ASEAN. * In recent years, a series of landmark infrastructure projects, including the China-Laos Railway and the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway in Indonesia, have been completed and put into operation, significantly enhancing regional connectivity, driving economic growth, and improving people's livelihoods. * "People are the makers and drivers of long-lasting relationships. Our partnership should be defined by peace, by our people, and by shared prosperity," ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn told Xinhua. by Xinhua writers Zhang Yisheng, Cao Kai JAKARTA, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- At the 29th China-ASEAN Summit held in the Philippine capital Manila, leaders from China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) welcomed the upcoming entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol on Dec. 1, encouraging businesses to fully seize the opportunities it brings. This year marks the 35th anniversary of their dialogue relations and the fifth anniversary of their comprehensive strategic partnership. Amid a complex and evolving international landscape, China-ASEAN cooperation has forged ahead against headwinds, achieving both quantitative growth and qualitative upgrades through strengthened strategic mutual trust, booming economic and trade ties, and vibrant people-to-people exchanges, scholars and experts have told Xinhua. STRATEGIC MUTUAL TRUST For a long time, China has remained committed to the principles of amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness in its neighborhood diplomacy to build a shared home of peace and prosperity with ASEAN countries. In November 2021, China and ASEAN elevated their ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership at a special summit commemorating the 30th anniversary of their dialogue relations. Over the past five years, leaders from both sides have continued their time-honored friendship, upheld the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and followed the trend of innovation and development. Today, China and ASEAN have established 66 cooperation mechanisms across various fields and at all levels -- the highest number among all of ASEAN's dialogue partners, according to the Chinese Mission to ASEAN. Meanwhile, China has reached important common understanding with eight ASEAN member states on forming a community with a shared future bilaterally. "Over the past five years, under the strategic guidance of the leaders of both sides, China and ASEAN have taken the building of a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home as their shared vision," Chinese Ambassador to ASEAN Wang Qing told Xinhua in a recent interview. "This has guided China-ASEAN cooperation to stay at the forefront, advance steadily, and move at a fast pace, continuously deepening and substantiating the building of a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future," he added. Similarly, Humprey Arnaldo Russel, head of the ASEAN-China Research Center at the University of Indonesia, noted that ASEAN countries and China "have every reason to" continue their tradition of friendship, focus on shared interests and keep bilateral cooperation moving forward. SHARED PROSPERITY The vitality of China-ASEAN relations lies in shared interests and their ability to deliver tangible benefits to both sides. With the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol set to take effect in December, more opportunities will emerge for businesses to make long-term plans, expand investment, and strengthen cooperation. In recent years, a series of landmark infrastructure projects, including the China-Laos Railway and the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway in Indonesia, have been completed and put into operation, significantly enhancing regional connectivity, driving economic growth, and improving people's livelihoods. China has remained ASEAN's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, while ASEAN has been China's largest trading partner for six years in a row. Bilateral trade surpassed 1 trillion U.S. dollars for the first time in 2025. As of July this year, both the cumulative two-way investment between China and ASEAN and the cumulative turnover of Chinese enterprises' contracted projects in ASEAN have exceeded 515 billion dollars. As a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation accelerates, digital and green transitions are reshaping regional industrial development, unlocking vast potential for cooperation in emerging sectors. For instance, the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement was signed on Nov. 14, marking a major milestone in the 11-member bloc's journey toward an open, secure, interoperable, competitive and inclusive digital economy. "ASEAN's expanding market demand and advantages in resource endowments can be aligned with and complement China's accumulated experience in cross-border e-commerce, mobile payments, and cloud computing, bringing immense opportunities for China-ASEAN cooperation," Wang said. The prospects for China-ASEAN digital economy cooperation are promising, said Lye Liang Fook, associate senior fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore. Lye suggested that both sides step up efforts to build secure digital infrastructure, such as 5G networks and undersea cables, backed by reliable renewable energy supplies, while accelerating cross-border digitalization through electronic certificates and documents to lower transaction costs for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for over 90 percent of all businesses in Southeast Asia. GOOD NEIGHBORS Connected by mountains and rivers with deep cultural affinity, China and ASEAN countries have been bound by strong people-to-people ties. Multiple public opinion polls have shown a steady rise in mutual goodwill and widespread optimism regarding the prospects of China-ASEAN relations. As ASEAN prepares to celebrate its 60th anniversary in 2027, ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn told Xinhua earlier this year that people-to-people connectivity and mutual trust will remain fundamental to the future of ASEAN-China relations. "People are the makers and drivers of long-lasting relationships. Our partnership should be defined by peace, by our people, and by shared prosperity," Kao said. "Trust is always the most powerful factor in our relationship, and we must focus on it as the key to our long-term relations." Over the past five years, anchored by the China-ASEAN Year of People-to-People Exchanges, the two sides have built a multi-tiered exchange framework while rolling out visa facilitation measures, injecting fresh vitality into cultural interactions, according to the Chinese Mission to ASEAN. "People-to-people connectivity serves as the most foundational, solid, and enduring bond," Russel said, pointing out a growing trend of Indonesian students aspiring to pursue higher education in China. He added that maintaining the momentum of cultural and educational exchanges while expanding practical cooperation in tourism, media, youth and other fields will help cultivate lasting friendship for the future. "ASEAN will always be China's neighbor, and China will always be ASEAN's. I think we already have very strong and smooth cooperation, both with individual member states and with ASEAN as a whole. So going forward, this cooperation will certainly continue to strengthen," said Michael Tene, a senior Indonesian diplomat who had served as deputy secretary-general of ASEAN for the ASEAN Political-Security Community. "I remain very optimistic that we, ASEAN countries, will continue to enjoy deep cooperation with China, because it serves the mutual interests of both sides," Tene added. ■

item.title: China's stable development contributes to world peace, global governance: embassy official
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
LONDON, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- The fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has provided a solid political guarantee for advancing Chinese modernization, while China's stable development will continue to contribute to world peace and prosperity, a Chinese diplomat said in London on Thursday. Speaking at a press briefing, Bi Haibo, minister counsellor at the Chinese Embassy in Britain, said the plenary session had made strategic arrangements for exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance. Bi said the session was of great significance in strengthening Party unity, ensuring that Party members remain committed to their missions and responsibilities, maintain close ties with the people and work towards the common goal of Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Bi also said China's stability and development are in themselves "a contribution to world peace," adding that the country will continue to pursue stable and predictable development. China is committed to building a community with a shared future for humanity, he said, highlighting the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative as China's solutions to growing global uncertainties and instabilities. "These are also the initiatives arranged and implemented with concrete actions, measures rather than slogans," Bi said, stressing China's commitment to multilateralism, the WTO-centered multilateral trading system and making greater contributions to global peace and development. ■

item.title: Chinese business community urges U.S. to withdraw proposed tariffs
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese business community has urged the United States to withdraw its proposed additional tariffs on China and 13 other economies following a Section 301 investigation into alleged "structural excess capacity" in manufacturing sectors, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said Friday. The Office of the United States Trade Representative recently announced findings of its Section 301 investigation and proposed imposing additional tariffs on 14 economies, including China. "The Chinese business community firmly opposes this," a CCPIT spokesperson said, adding that the community rejects the claim of "structural excess capacity" as a false narrative and opposes the U.S. side using the allegation as a pretext to interfere in normal China-U.S. economic and trade exchanges. Assessments of industrial supply and demand conditions should take into account factors including global market demand, technological progress and investment cycles, the spokesperson said. Trade surpluses are shaped by multiple factors such as the international division of labor, market demand and macroeconomic conditions, and trade surpluses alone are insufficient to determine structural excess capacity. Tariff wars and trade wars benefit no one, the spokesperson said, adding that broad-based tariff hikes will push up procurement costs for U.S. downstream enterprises, place additional burdens on consumers and disrupt global industrial and supply chains. The Chinese business community calls on the United States to withdraw the proposed tariff measures and resolve relevant issues through consultations with China on the basis of equality, respect and mutual benefit, to maintain stable and sound China-U.S. economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said. The CCPIT will continue to follow the concerns of Chinese and U.S. enterprises and foster practical cooperation and communication among the business communities of China, the United States and other countries, the spokesperson added. ■

item.title: News Analysis: China's AI reality goes beyond market volatility
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- As valuations across the global artificial intelligence (AI) industry come under renewed scrutiny, China's AI sector has also experienced market swings, prompting questions about its growth prospects, with some even warning of a bubble on the verge of bursting. Yet such assessments risk conflating market volatility with the long-term trajectory of an entire industry, while overlooking a more fundamental question: Is meaningful progress of an industry defined by financial investment returns, or by technological advances and its ability to address real-world needs? Evidence from China's AI sector points to an industry with tangible momentum. In 2025, China's core AI industries were valued at over 1.2 trillion yuan (about 179 billion U.S. dollars), up 40 percent year on year, with the number of AI enterprises exceeding 6,200, according to industry authorities. More importantly, AI in China is moving rapidly out of the lab, to factory floors, logistics networks, power grids and hospitals. Official data showed that more than 30 percent of large industrial enterprises in China have adopted AI, and leading smart factories have embedded the technology in over 70 percent of their operations. While investors tend to focus on balance sheets, Chinese industries are looking at broader productivity gains. A September study by the International Labour Organization on AI adoption in Chinese enterprises found efficiency gains of 30 to 100 percent across core workflows. In smart manufacturing, production efficiency improvements reached 20 to 30 percent. The global uptake of Chinese AI models speaks to the sector's technological progress. On OpenRouter, a leading global AI platform, Chinese AI models recorded 119.1 trillion tokens in weekly usage between Nov. 9 and 15, ranking first worldwide for the 29th consecutive week. The open-source approach of Chinese models has offered cost-effective solutions for businesses worldwide. These advances have come despite an increasingly restrictive external environment. Expanding technology controls from the West have constrained Chinese firms' access to advanced AI chips, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related technologies. It highlights an inherent contradiction: If China's AI industry were merely a speculative bubble, what would explain the sustained efforts to contain its development as a strategic threat? External restrictions may raise costs, but are unlikely to derail China's AI development. While it still has considerable ground to make up in advanced AI chips and computing infrastructure, the country has laid out a clear strategic roadmap that makes AI a priority in its long-term development. In its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), China has called for breakthroughs in core AI technologies and the full implementation of the "AI Plus" initiative, which aims to integrate AI into technological innovation, industrial development and a wide range of economic and social activities. China is also well placed to turn these ambitions into reality. Backed by a vast domestic market, a dynamic industrial ecosystem, solid infrastructure and diverse application scenarios, the country is aiming to bring the scale of AI-related industries to over 10 trillion yuan by the end of 2030. China's vast power supply gives its AI industry another solid foundation for scaling up, as the country generates about one-third of the world's electricity and has built the world's largest and fastest-growing renewable energy system. The country has also been accelerating efforts to expand its computing capacity. Data from the National Data Administration showed that China's intelligent computing capacity reached 1.59 million PFLOPS at the end of 2025, ranking second globally. Meanwhile, closer coordination between computing infrastructure and energy supply is channeling more green power to AI development. Barriers that divide the global AI industry risk fragmenting technology ecosystems and undermining international cooperation. Against this backdrop, China's open-source AI models offer the developing world an affordable way to narrow the AI gap and harness the technology to boost productivity. The debate over China's AI industry points to a larger truth about the future of the technology: Progress is rarely linear, and the path forward will inevitably be uneven. Market enthusiasm may fuel its boom, but only continuous innovation and real-world applications can sustain it. China has both the industrial and technological foundation and momentum to carry this progress forward. Ultimately, the industry's trajectory will be shaped not by short-term market swings, but by its ability to exercise patience, keep innovation flowing across borders, and deliver lasting economic value for China and the wider world. ■

item.title: China's high-standard opening up creates new opportunities for global cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
* Despite a complex external environment, China's goods imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Imports rose 23.6 percent, continuing to outpace export growth amid China's ongoing efforts to advance voluntary and unilateral opening up. * From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services. * Beyond facilitating the flow of goods and production factors, China is steadily advancing its institutional opening up in terms of rules, regulations, management and standards, seeking closer alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules. BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- At Friendship Pass on the China-Vietnam border in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, an improved customs inspection system has cut the time needed to identify pests in imported fruit to 36 hours or less, down from three to five days. This port handled durian imports worth 17.61 billion yuan (about 2.62 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of 2026, up 27.9 percent year on year, with China and Vietnam now jointly developing a smart border port to further facilitate cross-border trade. These efforts reflect China's broader push to expand high-standard opening up and develop new competitive advantages, a theme explored in the latest episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency. BROADENING THE SCOPE OF OPENING UP Despite a complex external environment, China's goods imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Imports rose 23.6 percent, continuing to outpace export growth amid China's ongoing efforts to advance voluntary and unilateral opening up. The country's trading partners are becoming increasingly diverse. In the first three quarters of the year, China's goods trade with Belt and Road partner countries rose 17.1 percent year on year, accounting for 51 percent of its total trade in goods. Expanding into emerging markets has helped mitigate risks arising from slowing demand and mounting trade barriers in some traditional markets, making China's foreign trade more resilient, said Zhang Yan, a researcher at a research center under the National Development and Reform Commission. In northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, trade with Belt and Road partner countries surged 35.3 percent year on year in the first nine months, according to Li Kaiyi, head of Yinchuan Customs. To overcome the region's geographical constraints, local customs authorities have piloted a new customs supervision model for rail-sea intermodal transport, boosting logistics efficiency by more than 30 percent. Local customs authorities have also helped wine producers resolve difficulties in obtaining certificates for exports to the European Union, with the value of Ningxia's wine exports to Germany and Spain more than tripling in the first three quarters of 2026, Li said. The potential for cooperation extends beyond the wine industry. Speaking in Ningxia, New Zealand's ambassador to China pointed to opportunities for technical exchanges between the two countries in wine production, livestock farming and crop cultivation. China's opening up is also creating new opportunities for foreign investors. In Hainan Province in south China, the number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises rose 31.1 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, with new projects including a Siemens Energy gas turbine assembly base and service center, said Wang Fengli, deputy director of the Office of the Free Trade Port Working Committee of the Communist Party of China Hainan Provincial Committee. DEVELOPING NEW COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES China's advances in science and technology and the development of its digital economy are also creating new opportunities for international economic cooperation. From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services, Zhang said. The country's exports of knowledge-intensive services grew 11.7 percent year on year to 1.2 trillion yuan in the first three quarters of 2026, accounting for 53.7 percent of its total services exports. Opening-up policies are also helping develop new businesses in high-value-added services. In Hainan, for instance, bonded maintenance and expedited customs clearance can reduce aircraft maintenance costs for foreign airlines by around 10 percent to 15 percent, Wang said. Meanwhile, digital cultural products, including online literature, video games and online dramas, are another growing area in China's services exports, Zhang noted. In Hainan's Chengmai County, a public service platform helps game developers overcome barriers to international expansion, such as cross-border network latency, regulatory compliance and payment settlement. The platform has attracted 125 enterprises and has more than 40 million registered overseas users. Under the policies of the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) on secure and orderly cross-border data flows, this platform provides dedicated data links, reducing the costs developers would otherwise incur in arranging such connections themselves. DEEPENING INSTITUTIONAL OPENING UP Beyond facilitating the flow of goods and production factors, China is steadily advancing its institutional opening up in terms of rules, regulations, management and standards, seeking closer alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules. The Hainan FTP serves as a testing ground for such reforms. Following the launch of island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, the share of tariff lines eligible for zero-tariff treatment on qualifying imports increased from 21 percent to 74 percent, Wang said. At the regional level, the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol brings cooperation in the digital economy, green economy and supply chain connectivity into an institutional framework, moving regional cooperation beyond tariff reductions toward greater coordination of rules, Zhang said. Greater openness also requires stronger risk management capabilities, Zhang said, suggesting that pilot free trade zones and free trade ports conduct stress tests in areas like cross-border data flows, financial opening up and cross-border services trade. Looking ahead, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) sets out measures to further expand the areas and geographical scope of opening up in an orderly manner, promote innovation in trade, and attract and utilize more foreign investment. "Regardless of changes in the international landscape, China will continue to counter external uncertainties with the certainty of steadily expanding its voluntary opening up," Zhang said, adding that China's high-quality development will create new opportunities for countries around the world. ■
